error.auth.user_already_exists.message: Esiste già un account con questi dati.

error.auth.profile_not_found.context: HTTP 404 on GET/PATCH /v1/auth/profile and POST /v1/auth/password (slice S-C54): the presented credential is valid and names an account the directory no longer holds — a session outlives the account row it names when the account is deleted mid-session. The server is working correctly; the account is gone.

error.auth.profile_invalid.message: That display name cannot be used.
error.auth.profile_invalid.context: HTTP 400 on PATCH /v1/auth/profile (slice S-C54): the submitted display name is past the 128-character ceiling or carries control characters. Refused rather than silently rewritten — a name that renders as something other than what was typed is worse than one the server declines.

error.auth.password_invalid.context: HTTP 400 on POST /v1/auth/password (slice S-C54): the proposed new password is under the 12-character floor, or is the password already in use. The second case matters because a change that changes nothing leaves the caller believing a leaked credential has been rotated.

error.auth.current_password_invalid.message: That is not your current password.
error.auth.current_password_invalid.context: HTTP 403 on POST /v1/auth/password (slice S-C54): the current password presented to authorize the change did not match. 403 and not 401 — the caller is authenticated, and a 401 would send a client to a sign-in its live session does not need.

error.auth.totp_already_active.message: Two-factor authentication is already switched on.
error.auth.totp_already_active.context: HTTP 409 on POST /v1/auth/totp/enroll (slice S-C55): the account already has a confirmed second factor. Refused rather than silently replaced — an enroll that overwrote an active secret would let a stolen session swap the factor for one the attacker holds, without ever presenting a code.

error.auth.totp_not_pending.message: There is no two-factor setup waiting to be confirmed.
error.auth.totp_not_pending.context: HTTP 409 on POST /v1/auth/totp/verify-enrollment (slice S-C55): nothing is pending for this account — either enrolment was never started, or it was already confirmed.

error.auth.totp_not_enrolled.message: Two-factor authentication is not switched on for this account.
error.auth.totp_not_enrolled.context: HTTP 409 on POST /v1/auth/totp/disable (slice S-C55): there is no confirmed second factor to remove.

error.auth.totp_invalid_code.message: That code is not right. Check your authenticator app and try again.
error.auth.totp_invalid_code.context: HTTP 403 on the authenticated TOTP operations and 401 on POST /v1/auth/login/verify-totp (slice S-C55): the six-digit code did not verify, or it verified and had already been used. One answer for both — telling a caller that a code was correct but replayed would confirm they had the right code.

error.auth.totp_challenge_invalid.message: That sign-in has expired. Enter your password again.
error.auth.totp_challenge_invalid.context: HTTP 401 on POST /v1/auth/login/verify-totp (slice S-C55): the half-finished sign-in token did not verify, had expired, or was another kind of token. One answer for all three — a client can act on none of the distinctions and every one of them means starting the sign-in again.
